$comment: The workbook is source EVIDENCE and stays whole: every one of its 426 rows
survives export untouched, including the rows superseded below. What this
file records is the separate question of which canonical CUSTOMER products
those rows add up to, and it records it as reviewed data rather than as
conditionals scattered through the catalog build or the storefront.
Two ideas that were being used interchangeably, and are not the same:
SOURCE ROWS      what the workbook lists      426 (141 peptides)
CANONICAL VARIANTS what a customer can buy    424 (139 peptides)
Every decision below names the exact source rows it consumes, so the
provenance survives the merge and an operator can always get back to the
workbook rows that produced a canonical product.

why: The workbook carries this one 5 mg vial twice: GRP-0402 as Supplier
Catalog / Classification Pending, and GRP-0426 as RUO Research. They are
the same physical product, so rendering both would show a customer two
Hexarelin 5 mg rows at two different prices.
Production already adjudicated this: the 2026-08-19 retail release set
the active price to $49.00 and superseded $62.50, which is the RUO row's
price. The classification simply never followed the price.
Canonical result is the RUO row. GRP-0402 is kept as provenance.
Identical shape to Hexarelin. GRP-0407 is the pending row, GRP-0425 the
RUO row, and production already carries $59.00 active with $107.50
superseded from the same 2026-08-19 release.
Canonical result is the RUO row. GRP-0407 is kept as provenance.

commerceHolds.specification: CJC-1295 WITH DAC + IPAMORELIN 5 mg total
why: The workbook classifies this row RUO Research, which under the direct
purchase rule would make it Buy Now. The founder is holding it because
the exact component split between CJC-1295 (with DAC) and Ipamorelin
inside a 5 mg total is not confirmed, and nobody may invent it.
Recorded as a HOLD rather than by editing the workbook's channel to
Classification Pending, because the classification is not in doubt — the
formulation is. Falsifying the source to obtain a behaviour would lose
that distinction and would quietly reverse the next time the workbook is
re-exported.
Removing this entry is all that is needed to release it. No storefront
change, no code change.

expected.$comment: Asserted by the applier, so a silent drift fails the build rather than the storefront.
